title: Apple AirTag 2 Four-Pack Returns to Record-Low $89 on Amazon
excerpt: The second-generation item tracker is back at its Prime Day price, working out to roughly $22 per tag — a deal tailor-made for travelers heading into peak summer season.
body:
• Apple's AirTag 2 four-pack is back to $89 on Amazon, matching the all-time low first set during Prime Day in late June.
  • At roughly $22 per unit, the second-gen tracker is now cheaper per tag than the original AirTag at its regular $29 retail price.
  • Upgraded Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by 1.5 times, while a 50-percent louder speaker and Apple Watch support improve real-world tracking.
  • A Share Item Location feature works with more than 50 airline partners, letting travelers share luggage-tracker data directly with carriers.

Apple's AirTag 2 four-pack has dropped back to $89 on Amazon, matching the all-time low price first recorded during Prime Day in late June. The $10 discount off the $99 retail price may look modest at first glance, but it brings the effective per-unit cost down to about $22 — less than the single first-generation AirTag cost at full retail.

The deal is the same one that surfaced when Amazon ran its four-day Prime Day event from June 23 to 26. That promotion briefly expired, returned for Fourth of July sales, and has now reappeared as of this week, according to MacRumors. The single-pack AirTag 2 is also available at a slight discount, listed at $27, down from $29.

What's New in the Second Generation

Apple launched the AirTag 2 on January 26, 2026, keeping the same $29 single-unit and $99 four-pack pricing as its predecessor. Under the hood, a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by roughly 1.5 times compared to the original, according to Gizmodo. That means the directional arrows and distance readouts that guide users to a lost item activate from farther away — a meaningful improvement for locating a suitcase in a crowded airport carousel.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xo6dPEhTRTo

The built-in speaker is 50 percent louder with a redesigned chime, making it easier to hear an AirTag buried in a bag or tucked between couch cushions. Apple also made the speaker harder to remove — a direct response to reports that bad actors were disabling the anti-stalking alert sound on first-generation models.

Perhaps the most practical upgrade for everyday use is Precision Finding support on Apple Watch. The original AirTag required an iPhone to access step-by-step directional tracking. Now, if your phone itself is the item you have misplaced, the feature works from your wrist.

Why Travelers Are Paying Attention

AirTags have become standard packing-list items for frequent flyers, and the second generation leans further into that use case. A new Share Item Location feature lets users temporarily share an AirTag's real-time location with trusted contacts or, critically, with airline partners. Apple has signed up more than 50 airlines, enabling travelers to share tracker data directly with the carrier when checked luggage goes missing.

For members of the Indian diaspora who regularly fly long-haul routes between the United States and India, the feature addresses a persistent pain point. Lost or delayed luggage on multi-leg international itineraries is common, and having precise, shareable location data can speed up recovery with airlines and ground handlers. At $22 per tracker, equipping every checked bag for a family trip home is a straightforward investment.

Battery, Build, and Limitations

The AirTag 2 uses a standard CR2032 coin-cell battery rated for over a year of use. Apple says the enclosure now incorporates 85 percent recycled plastic, and all packaging is 100 percent fiber-based. It remains an Apple-ecosystem-only device — there is no Android support for Find My, so the tracker's full feature set works exclusively with iPhones and iPads running iOS 14 or later.

How Long Will the Deal Last?

Deal trackers at 9to5Toys noted that the AirTag 2 had seen "almost no discounts" outside Prime Day promotions. With both Fourth of July sales and Prime Day now over, Amazon has limited incentive to keep the price at $89 indefinitely. Historically, record-low Apple accessory prices during post-sale windows tend to revert within days once inventory stabilizes.

Shoppers weighing the purchase should note that the next major sale cycle — back-to-school promotions and the run-up to Amazon's fall Prime Big Deal Days — is still months away. For anyone planning summer travel, this may be the best window to stock up before prices return to full retail.
